features.text: The patient is a 35-year-old male.
The patient has had back pain for a couple of years.
The back pain started after falling on his back playing basketball.
The back pain is rated as a seven or eight on the pain scale.
The patient experiences pain radiating down the leg and numbness in the toes.
The patient had an MRI showing disk desiccation, a bulge with herniation, and radiculopathy at L4-L5.
The patient has no prior surgeries.
The patient has no chronic conditions other than back pain.
The patient took some white pills for pain but does not remember the name or type.
The patient received injections for back pain but does not remember the type or purpose.
The injections did not provide significant relief.
The patient experienced numbness in the toes, described as tingling or pins-and-needles.
The patient experiences weakness in the legs, especially on the left side, when standing for too long.
The patient had an incident of bowel incontinence, but it was not consistent.
The numbness in the toes is intermittent, sometimes tingling or pins-and-needles, and sometimes absent.
The patient experiences leg weakness, especially on the left side, when standing for prolonged periods.
The patient had a single incident of bowel incontinence, likely due to standing up too fast or dehydration.
The weakness in the legs is primarily on the left side and not bilateral.
The numbness in the toes is intermittent and not constant.
The patient had a single incident of bowel incontinence and has not experienced it since.
The numbness in the toes is random and not consistently triggered by specific activities or positions.
Lying on the side helps with back pain but may not affect the numbness in the toes.
The numbness and tingling in the toes and left leg radiate from the back, especially on the left side.
The numbness and tingling in the toes and left leg are not constant but are connected to back pain.
Lying on the side helps with back pain, but the patient is unsure if it affects the numbness in the toes.
The patient has not noticed any specific activities or positions that trigger or alleviate the numbness or tingling.
The patient has not noticed any changes in the pattern of symptoms over the past few months.
